newsitem.title: CANADA: Sherritt tops actives on investor speculation.
newsitem.headline: Sherritt tops actives on investor speculation.

text.p: Trading in Sherritt International Corp was bustling on the Toronto Stock Exchange Monday morning as investors speculated about how the company would spend its recently raised funds, analysts said.
More than 2.8 million shares traded hands in morning trading, pushing the stock up C$0.10 to C$8.55. The stock topped the Toronto Stock Exchange's most-actives list.
Investors were still reacting to Sherritt's C$675-million debenture issue announced a week ago, said mining analyst Julian Baldry at Nesbitt Burns in Toronto.
"It's the debenture and in addition it's the speculation on how the cash will be utilized," he said in a phone interview.
The company will say only that the proceeds will be used to finance capital projects, expand its existing businesses and pursue investments in Cuba.
"You don't know the opportunities that are being presented but it's obvious that the company is going to make a major acquisition," Baldry said.
"They must have something in mind or it would not have raised this amount of cash."

While Sherritt is known mainly for its nickel operations in Cuba, an acquisition would likely be an expansion into a different industry there since the nickel operations are not in need of more cash, Baldry said.
Sherritt is also involved in sugar, petroleum refining, real estate and communications on the island.
Trading in Sherritt stock seemed to ignore the drop in nickel prices on Monday.

Nickel was at a two-year low on the London Metal Exchange on Monday, driven down by speculative chart-based sales and weak fundamentals. LME inventories have risen steadily in the past few months because of a glut in stainless steel scrap and inventories of Russian nickel in Europe.
Shares in nickel giant Inco Ltd fell C$1.45 to C$45.10 by midday on Monday, but rival Falconbridge Ltd rose C$0.20 to C$31.25.
